hero.headline: First Windows PC powered by Nvidia chips set to debut next week
hero.body:
The first Windows personal computer powered by Nvidia processors will be unveiled next week, according to a report from Axios. The device will use Nvidia's new N1X laptop processors, developed in partnership with Microsoft and Arm.

Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm have all posted cryptic messages on social media ahead of the announcement, which is expected to take place at Nvidia's GTC event. The messages appear to be coordinated teasers for the new Arm-powered Windows PC chip.

The development marks a significant shift in the PC market, where Intel and AMD have long dominated the processor space for Windows machines. Nvidia, best known for its graphics processing units, has been expanding its chip design capabilities beyond GPUs.

The new N1X processors represent Nvidia's entry into the market for central processing units designed for laptops running Microsoft's Windows operating system. The chips are built on Arm architecture, the same technology used in many smartphones and tablets.

Arm-based processors have been gaining traction in the PC market in recent years, offering potential advantages in power efficiency compared to traditional x86 processors. Apple successfully transitioned its Mac computers to Arm-based chips starting in 2020, demonstrating the viability of the architecture for laptop and desktop computing.

The timing of the announcement suggests Nvidia aims to establish itself as a major player in the PC processor market. The company's existing strengths in artificial intelligence and graphics processing could give its laptop chips distinctive capabilities, though specific performance details have not been disclosed.

Microsoft's involvement in the partnership is significant, as the company's support will be essential for ensuring Windows software runs smoothly on the new Nvidia processors. The collaboration between Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm represents a coordinated effort to introduce a new option for Windows PC manufacturers and consumers.

cards.headline: US military disables ship attempting to breach Iran blockade
cards.body:
The United States military attacked and seized an Iranian-flagged container ship that tried to bypass an American blockade near the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first such interception since the blockade began last week. Iran's joint military command said the country would respond to what it called an act of piracy that violated a ceasefire in place since April 8.

US Central Command said marines departed the USS Tripoli assault ship by helicopter and rappelled onto the Touska on Sunday. President Trump posted on social media that a US Navy guided missile destroyer had warned the vessel to stop in the Gulf of Oman, but the ship did not comply. "Our Navy ship stopped them right in their tracks by blowing a hole in the engine room," Trump said, noting that US marines now had custody of the vessel.

Video posted by the US Defence Department showed the interception, including audio of the container ship's crew being warned they would face disabling fire if they refused to stop. A US sailor can be heard saying "Vacate your engine room. We're prepared to subject you to disabling fire." The video then shows the USS Spruance firing on the Touska near Iran's border with Pakistan.

Trump said the ship was under US Treasury sanctions due to prior illegal activity. The Touska had left Port Klang, a major port in Malaysia, before attempting to move past the US blockade, according to tracking information from TankerTrackers.com.

A spokesperson for Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya military command centre said: "We warn that the armed forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran will soon respond and retaliate against this armed piracy and the US military."

The incident throws into question Trump's earlier announcement that US negotiators would travel to Pakistan on Monday for another round of talks with Iran. That had raised hopes of extending the fragile ceasefire set to expire by Wednesday, but Iran has not confirmed it will attend.

Iranian state media reported that Tehran had rejected new peace talks for now, citing the ongoing blockade, threatening rhetoric, and Washington's shifting positions and excessive demands. This comes after Trump requested edits to a framework agreement his negotiating team had developed with Iran, particularly focusing on the fate of Iran's uranium stockpile.

The escalating standoff threatens to deepen the global energy crisis and push the two countries toward renewed fighting. The conflict has killed at least 3,000 people in Iran, nearly 2,300 in Lebanon, 23 civilians and 15 soldiers in Israel, and more than a dozen in Gulf Arab states. Thirteen US service members have also been killed.

cards.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran deal negotiated by his envoys
cards.body:
President Trump asked for several amendments to an agreement his envoys reached with Iranian counterparts during a meeting on Friday, according to administration officials briefed on the matter.

The request has triggered another round of negotiations between the parties that could extend several days. U.S. officials said Trump wants to finalize the deal but seeks to strengthen certain provisions, particularly those involving Iran's nuclear material and program.

The tentative agreement would extend the current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping lane. The two sides reached the preliminary framework this week, though final approval from both Trump and Tehran remains pending.

Trump announced on Friday that he had spoken with leaders from multiple countries about the deal, including officials from Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Egypt, Jordan, Bahrain, Turkey, and Pakistan. He also discussed the matter with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Trump stated on his social media platform that "an agreement has been largely negotiated" and that "final aspects and details" would be announced shortly.

According to reports, details of the proposed agreement include opening the Strait of Hormuz without tolls during a 60-day ceasefire extension, allowing Iran to sell oil freely, and holding negotiations on Iran's nuclear program over 30 to 60 days. In exchange, the United States would lift its blockade on Iranian ports.

However, Iran's state media reported conflicting positions. Iran's Fars news agency, close to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, stated that Iran would retain control of the Strait of Hormuz, including determining passage routes, timing, and methods. The agency said Trump's assertion that an agreement was nearly final was "inconsistent with reality."

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif later congratulated Trump on his peace efforts and indicated that Pakistan hoped to host another round of talks between the U.S. and Iran very soon. Pakistan's Army Chief Syed Asim Munir has been a key figure in the negotiations, holding recent meetings in Tehran with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

The negotiations come as the U.S. military maintains a naval blockade of Iranian ports. The diplomatic efforts involve multiple U.S. officials, including special envoy Steve Witkoff and adviser Jared Kushner, working to address Trump's specific concerns.

The ongoing discussions signal that while both sides have made progress toward an agreement, significant differences remain. Trump has indicated he will only accept a deal "where we get everything we want," and has continued threatening military strikes if negotiations fail.

cards.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes on Florida launchpad hours after receiving national security contract
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a static fire test at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida on Thursday night, destroying the launchpad at Launch Complex 36. The explosion occurred at 9pm ET and sent a massive fireball across the space coast, with the orange glow visible as far south as Fort Pierce, 115 miles away. Shockwaves from the blast were felt by residents in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach, and people hundreds of miles north in South Carolina reported seeing the glow in the sky.

The timing of the explosion proved particularly unfortunate for Blue Origin. On Tuesday, just hours before the test, NASA announced that the company had won a national security launch contract. The task order represented confidence in Blue Origin's capabilities as a provider for critical government missions.

Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos confirmed that all company employees were accounted for and safe. He described the day as "very rough" on social media but pledged to rebuild and return to flying. The company called the explosion an "anomaly" and said an investigation into the root cause was already underway.

The New Glenn rocket was designed to be a heavy-lift launch vehicle capable of carrying large payloads to orbit. Blue Origin intended to use this rocket to launch lunar landers for NASA's moon exploration program, including the landers that will transport astronauts to the lunar surface. The loss of this rocket now threatens NASA's ambitious timeline.

NASA announced plans on Tuesday for Blue Origin to launch the first of three planned missions this year to begin construction of a 20 billion dollar moon base. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman stated that a full evaluation of the program timeline would be conducted following the explosion. He acknowledged that "spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult."

This represents the latest setback for Blue Origin in its competition with SpaceX for NASA contracts. Last month, a payload from the third flight of New Glenn ended up in the wrong orbit, leading the Federal Aviation Administration to temporarily ground the rocket. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared the rocket to resume flights.

Blue Origin and SpaceX are both competing to support NASA's Artemis program, which aims to return humans to the moon. NASA plans to evaluate both companies' lunar landers during the Artemis III mission in 2027, which will determine which system ferries astronauts to the lunar surface during the subsequent Artemis IV mission planned for 2028.

Elon Musk, SpaceX's owner, briefly commented on the explosion on social media, saying "Most unfortunate" and adding that "Rockets are hard."

cards.headline: Federal judge to review Trump's $1.8 billion fund for prosecutorial targets
cards.teaser: A judge agreed to review the administration's fund that has sparked backlash and exposed divisions within the Republican Party.
cards.body:
A federal judge has reopened Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service after receiving a motion challenging a $1.8 billion settlement. The motion argues the settlement "is a product of collusion and is itself a fraud on the court." Judge Kathleen Williams in Miami is reviewing the case.

The settlement stems from Trump's original $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS following the leak of his personal and business tax returns by a former contractor. The reopened case will examine the legal validity of the fund that Trump's administration characterized as an anti-weaponization measure.

cards.headline: Judge orders Trump to address fraud allegations in IRS settlement case
cards.teaser: A federal judge directed Trump to answer questions about whether a settlement creating an anti-weaponization fund constituted fraud.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Miami has reopened President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS following a motion from a third party. The motion claims that the settlement agreement establishing Trump's $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" fund is "a product of collusion and is itself a fraud on the court."

The original lawsuit was filed by Trump and his sons after their personal and business tax returns were leaked by a former IRS contractor. The reopened case will examine whether the settlement was reached through proper legal procedures and whether the fund itself represents fraudulent activity. The fund has generated significant controversy since its announcement, creating divisions within the Republican Party.

cards.headline: 11 workers killed in Washington paper mill chemical tank implosion
cards.teaser: Officials have recovered and identified the remains of all nine workers who were initially missing after a deadly industrial accident.
cards.body:
Officials in Longview, Washington recovered and identified the remains of all nine workers who had been missing after a chemical tank implosion at a Nippon paper mill. The total death toll from the incident reached 11 workers.

Authorities are investigating the cause of the chemical tank implosion that led to the deaths. The disaster at the paper mill represents one of the deadliest industrial accidents in recent years. All victims have now been identified and their families notified.

hero.headline: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo kills more than 245
hero.body:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed at least 65 confirmed people, with 246 suspected cases reported across the conflict-affected Ituri province. The disease has also spread to neighboring Uganda, where a 59-year-old man died after traveling from the DRC.

The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, a particularly concerning development since no licensed vaccine currently exists for this variant. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention confirmed the virus in 13 of 20 samples tested by the DRC's national research laboratory. Previous Bundibugyo outbreaks occurred in 2007 and 2012.

Cases have been concentrated in the Mongwalu and Rwampara health zones, with additional suspected cases in neighboring Bunia. The World Health Organization estimates the death rate for confirmed cases at between 30 and 50 percent, which officials describe as extremely high.

Geographic challenges complicate containment efforts. Ituri province contains mining towns where population movement is constant, creating ideal conditions for disease spread. The region also shares borders with Uganda and South Sudan, raising concerns about transmission across international boundaries. The Africa CDC is coordinating urgent meetings with authorities from the DRC, Uganda, South Sudan, and the WHO to develop a regional response strategy.

Uganda's health ministry confirmed cases within its borders following the death of the traveler from Kampala. Dr. Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa CDC, emphasized that rapid coordination among neighboring countries is essential. He stated that the organization stands "in solidarity with the government and people of the Democratic Republic of the Congo as they respond to this outbreak."

The WHO chief visited the affected region to support containment efforts. Medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières described the situation as deeply alarming, particularly due to the rapid geographic spread of cases.

The Democratic Republic of Congo has experienced 16 Ebola outbreaks since the virus was identified there in 1976. However, the Bundibugyo strain's lack of an available vaccine distinguishes this outbreak from previous episodes. The country's healthcare system faces ongoing resource constraints that complicate epidemic response and treatment capacity.

Dr. Michael Head, a senior research fellow in global health at the University of Southampton, noted that the DRC likely experiences regular outbreaks due to multiple intersecting factors. These include close contact between humans and animal reservoirs, particularly bats, combined with population movement between rural and urban areas, tropical climate conditions, and extensive rainforest coverage.

Health workers and international organizations are establishing treatment centers and distributing protective equipment to staff. The situation remains fluid as authorities continue identifying and confirming additional cases across affected regions.

cards.headline: Rescuers free four more men trapped in flooded Laos cave
cards.teaser: Four men were freed from a flooded cave in Laos as rescue operations continue for two people still missing.
cards.body:
Divers have rescued four more men from a flooded cave in Laos where they had been trapped for 10 days. The men were among seven villagers who entered the cave system on May 20 while searching for gold. One person was rescued on Friday, followed by these four additional survivors.

Two people remain missing as rescue operations continue. Divers are navigating through narrow, water-filled tunnels and sharp rocks to reach them. The rescue effort has involved draining water from the cave and managing collapse hazards to safely extract the trapped miners.

cards.headline: Hundreds arrested in France after Paris Saint-Germain Champions League win
cards.teaser: French police arrested hundreds of people as crowds celebrating PSG's Champions League victory over Arsenal turned unruly.
cards.body:
Paris Saint-Germain retained the Champions League title with a shootout victory over Arsenal. The win sparked celebrations across France that descended into unrest.

Thousands of police officers were deployed to manage crowds as fans gathered in multiple locations. Some supporters fired flares during the festivities, and authorities worked to control the disturbances. Hundreds of people were arrested as the celebrations escalated.

cards.headline: Drone crashes into apartment building in eastern Romania
cards.teaser: A drone struck an apartment building in eastern Romania, bringing the Russia-Ukraine war close to Romanian homes.
cards.body:
A drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania, causing a loud explosion and fire. The incident reminded residents of the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war and the dangers of living near the conflict zone.

Residents experienced panic following the crash. The proximity of the war to Romania has created ongoing security concerns for people living in border regions.

cards.headline: Israeli soldiers describe ongoing operations in Gaza despite ceasefire
cards.teaser: Israeli soldiers gave rare firsthand accounts of continuing military actions in Gaza, calling the ceasefire agreement ineffective.
cards.body:
Israeli soldiers have provided rare public accounts to the Associated Press describing military operations continuing in Gaza despite an announced ceasefire. Multiple soldiers disputed the ceasefire's validity, stating that indiscriminate killings persist in the territory.

An Israeli commander separately shared intelligence assessments regarding Hezbollah, indicating the militant group had planned attacks comparable to those carried out by Hamas. These soldier testimonies offer uncommon direct witness accounts of current conditions and military activities in Gaza.

cards.headline: Ecuador offers to cancel tariffs for Colombian presidential candidate
cards.teaser: Ecuador's president offered to eliminate tariffs after speaking with a right-wing Colombian candidate ahead of Sunday's election.
cards.body:
Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa has offered to cancel tariffs after speaking with a right-wing presidential candidate in Colombia. The proposal was made just before Colombians voted in their presidential election on Sunday.

Colombia has accused Ecuador of election interference through the tariff offer, viewing it as an attempt to influence voters ahead of the polls.

cards.headline: Iranian soccer team practices in Turkey while awaiting U.S. visas for World Cup
cards.teaser: Iran's national soccer team is training in Turkey and developing contingency plans while waiting for American visas.
cards.body:
The Iranian national soccer team continues training sessions in Turkey while awaiting U.S. visa approval for World Cup participation. Players are preparing contingency plans in case travel documentation issues prevent them from competing.

The visa delays coincide with regional tensions and ongoing military conflict. Team officials are working to resolve the administrative obstacles that could affect Iran's World Cup participation.

cards.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran peace framework negotiated by his envoys
cards.teaser: President Trump has sent tougher terms back to Iran after his negotiating team developed an initial peace framework.
cards.body:
President Trump met with his advisers to make a "final determination" on an Iran peace deal framework that U.S. and Iran officials had agreed to. Trump requested edits to the agreement, particularly regarding provisions about Iran's uranium stockpile, according to officials who confirmed he sent tougher terms back to Iran after reviewing his team's initial proposal.

The negotiations come as both sides work toward a potential resolution to end the conflict. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has discussed the ongoing talks publicly as Trump considers whether to accept the framework.

cards.headline: ICE agent arrested in Texas for shooting during Minnesota immigration raid
cards.teaser: An ICE agent has been arrested and charged in connection with a shooting that occurred during an operation in north Minneapolis.
cards.body:
An Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent was arrested in Texas on charges related to a shooting in north Minneapolis. The agent had been charged in connection with the shooting of a Venezuelan man during an immigration raid conducted as part of Operation Metro Surge.

The shooting occurred in January during the immigration enforcement operation. The agent faces criminal charges for the incident that took place in Minnesota. Authorities arrested the agent in Texas after charges were filed.

cards.headline: Bus driver charged after crash kills family of four traveling to wedding in Virginia
cards.teaser: Five people died in a Virginia crash, including a family of four who were traveling to attend a wedding.
cards.body:
A bus driver has been charged following a crash in Virginia that killed five people, including a family of four who were traveling to a wedding. The fatal accident resulted in criminal charges against the driver responsible for the bus.

The family of four was among those who died in the collision. A fifth person also lost their life in the crash. Authorities filed charges against the bus driver after investigating the circumstances of the accident.

cards.headline: Detainees sue federal government over conditions at Texas ICE facility
cards.teaser: Immigrant detainees filed a lawsuit accusing the government of inhumane treatment at a facility in El Paso.
cards.body:
A class-action lawsuit has been filed against Immigration and Customs Enforcement alleging severe violations of human and constitutional rights at Camp East Montana, the largest immigration detention facility in the United States. Four detainees are named as plaintiffs representing all current and future civil detainees at the El Paso, Texas facility.

The complaint lists multiple allegations including abhorrent medical and mental health care, inappropriate use of force, indiscriminate solitary confinement, inadequate food, disease outbreaks, unsanitary living conditions, and sexual harassment by guards. Legal organizations are pursuing the case on behalf of those held at the facility.

cards.headline: United Airlines flight diverted after passenger attempts to breach cockpit
cards.teaser: A 75-year-old man was arrested after attempting multiple times to reach the cockpit during a flight to Minneapolis.
cards.body:
A United Airlines flight traveling to Minneapolis was diverted to Madison, Wisconsin after a 75-year-old passenger attempted multiple times to enter the cockpit. The crew responded to the threat during the flight.

The aircraft landed safely in Madison where authorities took the passenger into custody. He was arrested following the incident.

cards.headline: SoftBank pledges up to $75 billion for AI data centers in France
cards.teaser: The Japanese conglomerate plans to build what would become Europe's largest artificial intelligence facility.
cards.body:
SoftBank announced plans to invest up to €75 billion to build AI data centers in France, creating what the company describes as Europe's biggest AI facility. CEO Masayoshi Son confirmed the commitment to the project.

The investment will develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity, focusing on artificial intelligence computing infrastructure as part of SoftBank's broader technology investments.

cards.headline: New car buyers drop by one million as affordability crisis deepens
cards.teaser: Auto sales have declined for eight consecutive months as rising prices push vehicles out of reach for many Americans.
cards.body:
One million fewer Americans are purchasing new cars, marking a significant contraction in the automotive market. The decline represents drivers who have exited the new vehicle market and are not expected to return soon.

Auto sales have fallen for eight straight months as prices remain elevated and consumer budgets tighten. Electric vehicle demand has collapsed alongside traditional car sales, compounding pressure on manufacturers and dealers across the country.

cards.headline: China's biotechnology industry grows as US worries about losing dominance
cards.teaser: Clinical trials in China are drawing attention at an international oncology conference in Chicago.
cards.body:
China's drug development sector is drawing international attention at an oncology conference in Chicago, where clinical trials conducted there are gaining prominence. The visibility underscores concerns among American officials and industry leaders about shifting global pharmaceutical leadership.

China's biotechnology industry has expanded significantly in recent years, bolstered by growing clinical trial infrastructure and research capabilities. This expansion is reshaping the competitive landscape and fueling worry that American dominance in biotechnology may be declining.

cards.headline: Ferrari faces criticism over first electric vehicle design
cards.teaser: The Luce, Ferrari's debut EV, has drawn backlash from critics who say it departs from the brand's heritage.
cards.body:
Ferrari's first electric vehicle, the Luce, has been met with heavy criticism following its unveiling. The Italian luxury carmaker designed the EV to compete with Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers.

Critics say the Luce represents an abandonment of Ferrari's traditional design philosophy and performance roots. The backlash has created questions about the brand's strategy as it enters the electric vehicle market.

cards.headline: Tech startups offer free cleaning in exchange for filming household chores
cards.teaser: Companies are paying workers to record themselves doing dishes and tidying up to train artificial intelligence systems.
cards.body:
A startup is offering to clean apartments for free if residents allow the work to be recorded on video. The company plans to use the footage to develop AI systems that can learn household tasks.

Multiple tech companies are now paying workers to film themselves performing routine chores. The recorded data helps train artificial intelligence models to recognize and potentially automate domestic work, though the workers themselves remain essential to the current data collection process.

cards.body:
SoftBank announced plans to invest up to €75 billion to build data centers in France. The company aims to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity in the country.

The investment represents a significant commitment to expanding digital infrastructure in France.

cards.headline: Nintendo releases backwards compatibility fixes for Switch games on Switch 2
cards.teaser: The company has issued a new wave of updates to improve how original Switch games run on its newer console.
cards.body:
Nintendo has released a new set of backwards compatibility fixes for Switch games running on the Switch 2. The updates address issues with how games designed for the original Switch perform on the newer hardware.

The release represents the latest wave of patches aimed at ensuring smooth operation of the existing Switch game library on the Switch 2 console. Nintendo has been working to maintain compatibility between the two systems.

cards.headline: GitHub Copilot switches to token-based billing, drawing developer criticism
cards.teaser: Microsoft's GitHub has ended its low-cost era of AI programming assistance and will now charge based on token usage.
cards.body:
GitHub announced it will move to token-based billing for its Copilot AI coding assistant, ending what some developers described as a golden age of affordable AI programming tools. The change marks a shift from the previous pricing model.

Developers have expressed frustration with the new billing structure, which ties costs to the number of tokens processed rather than a flat subscription fee. The change makes it harder for startup founders to predict and manage their AI coding costs.

cards.headline: Former Snap employees launch Ghost Angels fund for social media startups
cards.teaser: A group of 20 Snap alumni has created an investment fund to back the next generation of social media companies.
cards.body:
Twenty Snap alumni have launched Ghost Angels, an investment fund dedicated to backing the next generation of social media startups. The group leverages their experience from Snapchat's parent company to identify and support emerging social platforms.

This coordinated effort by Snap veterans represents a significant push from company insiders into early-stage venture investing within the sector they helped develop.

cards.headline: Newly discovered fungus may help restore habitats damaged by invasive moss
cards.teaser: Scientists have found a fungal species that could aid in recovering native British ecosystems overrun by non-native moss.
cards.body:
A newly discovered fungus species has raised hopes for restoring native British habitats that have been overtaken by invasive moss. The fungus appears to target the invasive moss, potentially providing a biological solution to ecosystem damage.

Researchers believe the discovery could offer a way to help native plant communities recover in areas where invasive moss has become established. The fungus represents a potential tool for habitat restoration efforts across affected regions.

cards.headline: Minecraft announces new biome coming this fall
cards.teaser: The game will add another environment type in its third content drop of the year.
cards.body:
Minecraft revealed plans to introduce a new biome to the game this fall during its TwitchCon 2026 event. The announcement was part of the Minecraft Live broadcast, which outlined upcoming content for the game.

The new biome will arrive as part of the game's third content drop scheduled for later this year. Minecraft also confirmed that its Chaos Cubed update will launch in June, ahead of the fall biome release.

hero.headline: Spurs defeat Thunder in Game 7, advance to NBA Finals
hero.body:
The San Antonio Spurs eliminated the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder with a 111-103 victory in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals on Saturday night. The win sends the Spurs to the NBA Finals to face the New York Knicks, with Game 1 scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio.

Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs to victory, marking his first appearance in the NBA Finals. The Thunder entered the season as reigning champions but could not complete a title defense after falling short in this playoff matchup.

"When we've got the best player in the world, things happen," said Julian Champagnie after the game. Champagnie contributed significantly to the victory, scoring 20 points for San Antonio.

While Wembanyama was instrumental in the win, the Spurs' success was built on contributions from multiple players. Champagnie's scoring prowess proved critical throughout the contest. Dylan Harper provided important production off the bench, making an impact whenever he entered the game. Luke Kornet, Wembanyama's backup, made a crucial defensive play in the fourth quarter with a brilliant block that prevented the Thunder from completing a comeback.

The Thunder mounted pressure as the final moments approached, forcing them to take desperate three-point attempts from well beyond the arc. However, the Spurs secured the series with a decisive breakaway dunk that sealed their advancement.

For much of the season, questions lingered about whether the Thunder possessed any weaknesses. Their roster appeared formidable as defending champions, but they lacked a player of Wembanyama's caliber. The Spurs' ability to deploy such a dominant talent at a young stage in his career proved to be the difference in this tightly contested series.

The loss ended Oklahoma City's hopes of returning to the Finals. Despite their championship pedigree and strong performance throughout the playoffs, the defending champions could not overcome San Antonio's superior talent and execution when it mattered most.

The Spurs will now prepare for their matchup against the Eastern Conference champion Knicks. San Antonio's path through the Western Conference bracket culminated in this Game 7 triumph, earning them the opportunity to compete for the NBA championship in the Finals series ahead.

Wembanyama's emergence as a player capable of leading his team to the Finals at such an early stage of his career signals a potential shift in the league's power structure. The Spurs' organization will look to build on this success and bring home a championship in the Finals.

cards.headline: Coco Gauff eliminated in third round at French Open
cards.teaser: Defending champion Coco Gauff lost to Anastasia Potapova in the third round at Roland Garros.
cards.body:
Coco Gauff's title defense at the French Open came to an end in the third round, losing to 28th seed Anastasia Potapova 4-6, 7-6 (1), 6-4. Despite taking the first set and leading by a break in the final set, Gauff faltered down the stretch, losing five of the last six games.

After the match, Gauff reflected on her performance in crucial moments, saying she failed to capitalize on her opportunities. She specifically cited missed backhands at 3-all in the third set when she had break points, calling those missed shots critical errors at such a pivotal stage of the match.

cards.headline: Finland defeats Canada to reach world championship final
cards.teaser: Finland will face Switzerland for gold at the world championships after beating Canada in the semifinals.
cards.body:
Finland advanced to the world championship final with a victory over Canada in the semifinal round. Aleksander Barkov led Finland past Canada to secure the finals berth.

The Finnish team will face Switzerland in the gold medal game. Canada's Sidney Crosby and Parker Wotherspoon were held pointless in the loss that ended their tournament run.

cards.headline: President Trump defends Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart
cards.teaser: President Trump responded to criticism of Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart after Dart introduced Trump at a rally.
cards.body:
President Trump defended New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart against critics following Dart's introduction of the president at a rally. Trump characterized the critics as jealous.

Giants players Jaxson Dart and Abdul Carter addressed the situation amid disagreement over Dart's appearance at the Trump event. Former NFL player Dez Bryant supported Dart's decision, expressing confusion about the criticism directed toward him.

cards.headline: Arsenal to hold title parade one day after Champions League final loss
cards.teaser: Arsenal will celebrate their Premier League title with an open bus parade despite losing the Champions League final.
cards.body:
Arsenal will celebrate their first Premier League title in 22 years with an open bus parade on Sunday, less than 24 hours after losing the Champions League final to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties. Kai Havertz's early goal gave Arsenal hopes of a domestic and European double, but PSG equalized through Ousmane Dembélé in the second half before the shootout decided the match. Gabriel Magalhães skied Arsenal's crucial penalty.

Manager Mikel Arteta acknowledged the heartbreak of the defeat but called on his players to convert that pain into motivation for next season. Despite falling short in Europe, Arsenal's Premier League success offers some consolation as the club continues its path back to domestic dominance.

cards.headline: Tennessee softball defeats Texas Tech in extra innings at WCWS
cards.teaser: Tennessee softball beat Texas Tech in extra innings at the Women's College World Series.
cards.body:
Tennessee softball defeated Texas Tech in extra innings during a Women's College World Series matchup. Clarke delivered a walk-off hit in extras against the Red Raiders.

Texas Tech now faces elimination after the loss to Tennessee. The seventh-seeded Tennessee team advanced in the WCWS bracket with the victory over the eleventh-seeded Red Raiders.

cards.headline: Darren Till wins BKFC debut with knockout of Aaron Chalmers
cards.teaser: Darren Till knocked out Aaron Chalmers in his Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship debut.
cards.body:
Darren Till made a successful transition to bare knuckle fighting, earning a knockout victory over Aaron Chalmers in his Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship debut. Till demonstrated resilience by bouncing back from an early knockdown to finish the fight with a devastating one-punch knockout.

The former mixed martial arts fighter's impressive performance showcased his ability to adapt to the bare knuckle format and deliver under pressure in his first bout with the promotion.

hero.headline: Search Suspended for Man Believed to Be Reality TV Star Matt Brown
hero.body:
Authorities in Alaska have suspended their search for a man believed to be Matt Brown, known from the Discovery Channel reality series Alaskan Bush People. Brown's brother Bear stated that Matt was spotted near a river where police say a man went missing.

According to family members, they fear Brown may have taken his own life. The 42-year-old appeared on Alaskan Bush People, which followed the Brown family living in remote areas of Alaska. He had been open about his struggles with substance abuse in recent years.

The search involved local law enforcement examining the area around the river where the man was last seen. Officials have not confirmed the identity of the missing person, though multiple family members have publicly connected the incident to Matt Brown.

Brown was one of the original cast members when the show premiered in 2014. He left the series in 2018 to enter rehabilitation treatment. The show documented the Brown family's attempts at self-sufficient living in the Alaskan wilderness, eventually moving to Washington state in later seasons.

The suspension of the search does not necessarily indicate the case is closed. Authorities sometimes halt active search operations due to safety concerns, weather conditions, or when immediate leads are exhausted. The family has been vocal on social media about their concerns for Matt's wellbeing in recent days.

Discovery Channel has not issued a statement regarding the situation. The show continued production after Brown's departure, focusing on other family members. His father, Billy Brown, died in 2021 at age 68.

Anyone struggling with suicidal thoughts can contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 988 for free, confidential support 24 hours a day.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remainder of Four Seasons Farewell Tour
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old singer cited health concerns in canceling the rest of his 2026 concert dates.
cards.body:
Frankie Valli has canceled the remaining dates of the Four Seasons' farewell tour due to health concerns. The 92-year-old music legend apologized to fans, expressing regret over disappointing them with the decision.

The canceled shows were scheduled for the rest of 2026. The Four Seasons rose to fame with classic hits like "Sherry" and "Big Girls Don't Cry."

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen Flips Piano Onstage After Technical Issue in Denver
cards.teaser: The country singer overturned an instrument during a performance after experiencing technical problems.
cards.body:
Morgan Wallen flipped a piano onstage during a Denver concert after the instrument malfunctioned while he was performing "Sand in My Boots." Video captured the moment showing Wallen's frustration with the technical glitch before he overturned the piano.

The incident disrupted his performance at the venue, drawing comparisons to similar on-stage instrument incidents in rock music history.

cards.headline: Trump to Headline Great American State Fair After Music Acts Cancel
cards.teaser: President Trump will appear at the event after several scheduled artists withdrew from performing.
cards.body:
President Trump plans to headline the Great American State Fair after multiple music acts canceled their performances. Trump has suggested canceling the concert portion of the event entirely and holding a rally instead.

Vanilla Ice defended his decision to perform at the Washington DC concert after nearly every other scheduled act backed out. Trump urged the cancellation of Freedom 250 concerts following the artist withdrawals. The Great American State Fair is part of celebrations planned for the nation's 250th anniversary.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Removes Cast Member Over Use of Racial Slur
cards.teaser: The show dismissed Vasana Montgomery after social media posts surfaced showing her using the n-word.
cards.body:
Love Island USA has removed cast member Vasana Montgomery from the upcoming season after social media posts revealed her use of the n-word. The show, set to premiere on Peacock on June 2, made the decision just two days before its scheduled launch.

This marks the second consecutive year that Love Island USA has dismissed an islander for using the racial slur on social media.

cards.headline: Niall Horan Reflects on Death of Former Bandmate Liam Payne
cards.teaser: The singer discussed memories of Payne, who died in 2024 after falling from a hotel in Argentina.
cards.body:
Niall Horan spoke about the death of his former One Direction bandmate Liam Payne in an interview with The Times of London. Payne died in 2024 at age 31 after falling three floors from a hotel in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Horan said the loss brings sadness but also makes him laugh because of the memories they shared. He revealed he was with Payne in Argentina shortly before his death. The two had performed together as part of the popular boy band One Direction before the group went on hiatus.

cards.headline: Warner Bros. Pictures Chief Warns Against Cutting Development Budgets
cards.teaser: Michael De Luca said studios risk drying up their pipeline by reducing funding for original material.
cards.body:
Warner Bros. Pictures chief Michael De Luca warned against drastic cuts to development budgets for original content during a master class at the Produced By conference, hosted by the Producers Guild of America. He cautioned that excessive budget reductions could deplete the creative pipeline.

De Luca stressed the importance of investing in new talent and fresh voices to sustain the pipeline—describing this as a guiding principle for studio leadership.

hero.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran deal negotiated by his envoys
hero.body:
President Trump asked for several amendments to an agreement his envoys reached with Iranian counterparts during a meeting on Friday, according to administration officials briefed on the matter.

The request has triggered another round of negotiations between the parties that could extend several days. U.S. officials said Trump wants to finalize the deal but seeks to strengthen certain provisions, particularly those involving Iran's nuclear material and program.

The tentative agreement would extend the current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping lane. The two sides reached the preliminary framework this week, though final approval from both Trump and Tehran remains pending.

Trump announced on Friday that he had spoken with leaders from multiple countries about the deal, including officials from Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Egypt, Jordan, Bahrain, Turkey, and Pakistan. He also discussed the matter with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Trump stated on his social media platform that "an agreement has been largely negotiated" and that "final aspects and details" would be announced shortly.

According to reports, details of the proposed agreement include opening the Strait of Hormuz without tolls during a 60-day ceasefire extension, allowing Iran to sell oil freely, and holding negotiations on Iran's nuclear program over 30 to 60 days. In exchange, the United States would lift its blockade on Iranian ports.

However, Iran's state media reported conflicting positions. Iran's Fars news agency, close to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, stated that Iran would retain control of the Strait of Hormuz, including determining passage routes, timing, and methods. The agency said Trump's assertion that an agreement was nearly final was "inconsistent with reality."

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif later congratulated Trump on his peace efforts and indicated that Pakistan hoped to host another round of talks between the U.S. and Iran very soon. Pakistan's Army Chief Syed Asim Munir has been a key figure in the negotiations, holding recent meetings in Tehran with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

The negotiations come as the U.S. military maintains a naval blockade of Iranian ports. The diplomatic efforts involve multiple U.S. officials, including special envoy Steve Witkoff and adviser Jared Kushner, working to address Trump's specific concerns.

The ongoing discussions signal that while both sides have made progress toward an agreement, significant differences remain. Trump has indicated he will only accept a deal "where we get everything we want," and has continued threatening military strikes if negotiations fail.

cards.headline: U.S. military disables ship attempting to breach Iran port blockade
cards.teaser: U.S. Central Command disabled a vessel flying under a Gambian flag after it ignored warnings while trying to dock at an Iranian port.
cards.body:
U.S. Central Command announced on Saturday that it had prevented another vessel from docking at an Iranian port amid a U.S. naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. military disabled a ship flying under a Gambian flag on Friday after the vessel did not heed numerous warnings, according to a statement.

The action occurred as the U.S. maintains its naval blockade of Iranian ports. The enforcement comes while negotiations continue between Washington and Tehran over a potential deal that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and extend the current ceasefire.

cards.headline: Federal judge to review Trump's $1.8 billion fund for prosecutorial targets
cards.teaser: A judge agreed to review the administration's fund that has sparked backlash and exposed divisions within the Republican Party.
cards.body:
A federal judge has reopened Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service after receiving a motion challenging a $1.8 billion settlement. The motion argues the settlement "is a product of collusion and is itself a fraud on the court." Judge Kathleen Williams in Miami is reviewing the case.

The settlement stems from Trump's original $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS following the leak of his personal and business tax returns by a former contractor. The reopened case will examine the legal validity of the fund that Trump's administration characterized as an anti-weaponization measure.

cards.headline: Lead prosecutor withdraws from James Comey criminal case
cards.teaser: The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against the former FBI director has stepped down from the case.
cards.body:
The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey has stepped down, according to a court filing. A notice of substitution filed in the Eastern District of North Carolina on Friday stated that Matthew, the lead prosecutor, would no longer represent the government in the case.

Comey faces charges for allegedly threatening the life of President Trump in a since-deleted social media post of seashells. The prosecutor's departure comes as the case continues through the federal court system.

cards.headline: New Jersey governor deploys state police to ICE detention center protests
cards.teaser: Gov. Mikie Sherrill sent state police to maintain order outside a Newark immigration facility after escalating protests.
cards.body:
New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill deployed state police outside the Delaney Hall immigration detention center in Newark, where protests have intensified. Detained immigrants at the facility launched a hunger and labor strike demanding improved conditions and medical care, which reached its ninth day by Saturday.

The scene turned contentious as counterprotesters wearing Trump hats and supporting ICE gathered outside to demonstrate. State police set up barricades to separate the rival groups as both sides chanted opposing slogans across the barrier.

cards.headline: Immigrant detainees sue federal government over Texas ICE facility conditions
cards.teaser: Detainees accuse the government of inhumane abuse and treatment at a facility in El Paso.
cards.body:
A class-action lawsuit was filed against Immigration and Customs Enforcement accusing the agency of severe violations at Camp East Montana in El Paso, Texas, the largest immigration detention facility in the United States. Four detainees are named as plaintiffs representing all current and future civil detainees at the facility.

The complaint details numerous allegations including abhorrent medical and mental health care, inappropriate use of force, indiscriminate solitary confinement, inadequate food, disease outbreaks, unsanitary living conditions, and sexual harassment by guards. Legal organizations filed the suit claiming conditions at the facility severely violate the human and constitutional rights of detainees.

cards.headline: Security preparations underway for America 250 celebrations in Washington
cards.teaser: Washington is preparing for commemorations of the nation's 250th anniversary as concerns about political violence persist.
cards.body:
Security preparations are underway across Washington ahead of celebrations commemorating the nation's 250th anniversary this summer. The first event, a UFC fight at the White House, will take place just weeks after a shooting outside the complex and two months after another incident.

The threat of political violence looms over the planned celebrations. Multiple events are scheduled throughout the summer to mark America 250, requiring coordination among federal and local law enforcement agencies.
